tagline: Norway's energy capital, the gateway to Preikestolen and Lysefjord, and a city with the wealth, the protected water and the 2026 zero-emission tailwind to lead foiling adoption.
summary: Stavanger is Norway's oil-and-energy capital — a wealthy, internationally connected city — and the gateway to Lysefjord, home of the Preikestolen (Pulpit Rock) and Kjerag, two of Norway's most visited natural landmarks. Tourist fjord cruises up Lysefjord, commuter ferries across to Strand/Tau and the surrounding islands, and a strong domestic boating culture combine with Norway's nation-leading marine-electrification programme and the 2026 zero-emission fjord trajectory. The protected Boknafjord/Lysefjord waters and the city's affluence and energy-transition identity make Stavanger a natural, well-funded launch theatre for fast clean foiling service.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: Stavanger's commuter and Lysefjord tourism legs — Tau/Strand (~8 nm), Forsand (~18 nm), Lysebotn (~35 nm) — all sit inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope on protected fjord water, with an affluent market and Norway's electrification tailwind behind them.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Extends to longer Boknafjord and outer-coast repositioning legs and any onward fjord cruising beyond the all-electric range, with no charging dependency.

competitive_landscape: Diesel fjord-cruise and ferry operators dominate today and face the same national decarbonisation pressure as the rest of Norway. Foiling differentiates on speed and ride-quality on top of zero emissions — and Stavanger's energy-transition self-image makes it an unusually receptive, well-capitalised host.
seasonality: Tourism peaks May-September with the Preikestolen hiking season; commuter and energy-sector demand is year-round. Sheltered fjord water keeps operations viable across seasons.
regulatory_note: Stavanger sits within Norway's national marine-electrification framework and the broader 2026 zero-emission fjord trajectory under the Norwegian Maritime Authority; clean propulsion enjoys strong policy and public support.
